correctness.rationale: The source gives 3tan²ω+2tan²γ=1 for the cone angle of the squared-side vector. Normalizing x=a²/N,y=b²/N,z=c²/N yields Σx=1 and (x−y)²+(y−z)²+(z−x)²=q², q²=(1−3tan²ω)/2<1/2; Heron implies every positive point of the circle is a strict triangle. In ordered chamber x≥y≥z>0 the fixed-q section is a connected compact arc. Its boundary y=z gives r_min=(1+√2 q)/(1−q/√2), while x=y has no lower ratio. The discriminant after x=rz gives (1−2q²)(r²+1)−2(1+q²)r≤0, with unique larger root r_max=(1+q²+q√(3(2−q²)))/(1−2q²), attained at y=(1+q²)/3 and x,z=((2−q²)/3±q√((2−q²)/3))/2. Symbolic independent calculations verified constraints and extrema; numerical q=0.4 gave κ_min≈1.4775597308, κ_max≈1.7572485219. At q=0 both equal one; q→1/√2 only limiting degeneracy and is excluded.

originality.rationale: Bényi–Ćurgus Proposition 4.1 supplies the cone/Brocard equivalence but not the constrained max/min longest-to-shortest side ratio. The later Hungerbühler–Zhang “Brocard families” constructs families sharing ω via fourth-power sum invariance; it does not optimize κ over all shapes. The submitted ordered-chamber endpoint and discriminant classification therefore adds an exact extremal interval that is not implied by these source theorems.
